What I changed (concrete)
- Renamed method deposite(...) to deposit(...).
- Added null-safety and input validation on the deposit endpoint:
  - Validates request body is present.
  - Validates accountId is non-empty.
  - Validates amount is non-null and > 0 (DTOs use BigDecimal).
  - Returns 400 BAD_REQUEST via ResponseStatusException for invalid inputs.
- Improved logging to avoid possible NullPointerExceptions by guarding against null request objects and response objects.
- Adjusted the deposit fallback logging to guard against nulls and removed any reference to missing fields.
- Removed unused imports (tracer, Autowired) and replaced with imports used for validation and HTTP status.
- Kept withdraw and transfer handlers mostly intact, but added null-safe logging (they already used service methods).

Why these changes
- The original had a typo in the public API method name (deposite) which is a breaking and confusing bug.
- Adding validation gives clearer error messages to clients and avoids NPEs or invalid service calls.
- Guarded logging prevents additional NPEs when requests are null or service returns null.
- Removing unused imports keeps the code clean.

Quick notes about DTOs and types
- I inspected DTOs (DepositRequest, WithdrawRequest, TransferRequest, TransactionResponse) and confirmed amount is BigDecimal — validation matches that.
- TransactionResponse is a Lombok builder and has status field; the fallback returns a FAILED status.
